claim: The P2X7 receptor is a trimeric, extracellular ATP-gated membrane channel expressed in many different cell types including immune and glial cells.
source: The P2X7 receptor is a trimeric, extracellular ATP-gated membrane channel expressed in many different cell types including immune and glial cells (Collo et al., 1997; Sluyter, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Collo et al., 1997 and Sluyter, 2017

claim: Activation of the P2X7 receptor allows small cations to traverse the plasma membrane.
source: Activation of the P2X7 receptor, like other P2X receptor subtypes (P2X1-6), allows small cations to traverse the plasma membrane, which triggers various intracellular signaling events such as gene expression (North, 2002; Habermacher et al., 2016; Di Virgilio et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to North, 2002; Habermacher et al., 2016; Di Virgilio et al., 2017

claim: Activation of the P2X7 receptor leads to the formation of a membrane pore that allows molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate upon ATP binding.
source: In particular, its activation leads to the formation of a membrane pore that allows molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate upon ATP binding (Steinberg et al., 1987; Di Virgilio, 1995; Surprenant et al., 1996; Alves et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Steinberg et al., 1987; Di Virgilio, 1995; Surprenant et al., 1996; Alves et al., 2014

claim: Heterologously overexpressed P2X7 receptors in various cell-lines take up organic cations such as ethidium and YO-PRO-1.
source: This unique characteristic is supported by a number of experiments from multiple labs where heterologously overexpressed P2X7 receptors in various cell-lines take up organic cations such as ethidium and YO-PRO-1 (Surprenant et al., 1996; Chessell et al., 1997; Rassendren et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to Surprenant et al., 1996; Chessell et al., 1997; Rassendren et al., 1997

claim: Macrophages derived from a P2X7 knockout mouse fail to take up dyes after ATP application.
source: Moreover, macrophages derived from a P2X7 knockout mouse fail to take up dyes after ATP application (Solle et al., 2001), highlighting that the P2X7 receptor is an essential component of the dye-permeable pore.
evidence: Supported by citation to Solle et al., 2001

claim: The P2X7 receptor is an essential component of the dye-permeable pore.
source: Moreover, macrophages derived from a P2X7 knockout mouse fail to take up dyes after ATP application (Solle et al., 2001), highlighting that the P2X7 receptor is an essential component of the dye-permeable pore.
evidence: Inferred from knockout mouse experiments cited in Solle et al., 2001

claim: The P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in proliferation of microglia.
source: This P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in multiple physiological and pathological events, including proliferation of microglia (Monif et al., 2009), colitic loss of enteric neurons (Gulbransen et al., 2012), and development of chronic pain (Sorge et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Monif et al., 2009

claim: The P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in colitic loss of enteric neurons.
source: This P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in multiple physiological and pathological events, including proliferation of microglia (Monif et al., 2009), colitic loss of enteric neurons (Gulbransen et al., 2012), and development of chronic pain (Sorge et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gulbransen et al., 2012

claim: The P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in development of chronic pain.
source: This P2X7 specific pore has been implicated in multiple physiological and pathological events, including proliferation of microglia (Monif et al., 2009), colitic loss of enteric neurons (Gulbransen et al., 2012), and development of chronic pain (Sorge et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sorge et al., 2012

claim: P2X7 alone is insufficient to form a dye-permeable pore.
source: This hypothesis is supported by the observations that (1) P2X7 alone is insufficient to form a dye-permeable pore (Petrou et al., 1997; Klapperstück et al., 2000)
evidence: Supported by citations to Petrou et al., 1997; Klapperstück et al., 2000

claim: P2X7 receptor expressing cells open two distinct pores for small and large ions.
source: (2) P2X7 receptor expressing cells open two distinct pores for small and large ions (Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Virginio et al., 1997; Faria et al., 2005; Jiang et al., 2005)
evidence: Supported by citations to Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Virginio et al., 1997; Faria et al., 2005; Jiang et al., 2005

claim: Heterologously expressed P2X7 receptors in the absence of Panx1 fail to open a dye-permeable pore.
source: (3) heterologously expressed P2X7 receptors in the absence of Panx1 fail to open a dye-permeable pore (Pelegrin and Surprenant, 2006)
evidence: Supported by citation to Pelegrin and Surprenant, 2006

claim: Panx1 inhibitors, but not P2X7 antagonists, block dye uptake.
source: (4) Panx1 inhibitors, but not P2X7 antagonists, block dye uptake (Locovei et al., 2007)
evidence: Supported by citation to Locovei et al., 2007

claim: P2X7 and Panx1 are co-immunoprecipitated in cell lysates derived from multiple cells.
source: (5) P2X7 and Panx1 are co-immunoprecipitated in cell lysates derived from multiple cells (Silverman et al., 2009; Li et al., 2011; Poornima et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Silverman et al., 2009; Li et al., 2011; Poornima et al., 2012

claim: Macrophages from a Panx1 knockout mouse normally take up YO-PRO-1.
source: However, this hypothesis has been challenged by other studies demonstrating that (1) macrophages from a Panx1 knockout mouse normally take up YO-PRO-1 (Qu et al., 2011)
evidence: Supported by citation to Qu et al., 2011

claim: Panx1 knockdown or Panx1 antagonists do not affect dye uptake.
source: (2) Panx1 knockdown or Panx1 antagonists do not affect dye uptake (Xu et al., 2012; Alberto et al., 2013)
evidence: Supported by citations to Xu et al., 2012; Alberto et al., 2013

claim: ATP actually antagonizes Panx1 activity.
source: (3) ATP actually antagonizes Panx1 activity (Qiu and Dahl, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Qiu and Dahl, 2009

claim: There is a tight correlation between the charge and accessibility of the pore-lining residues and permeability of the permeant dyes.
source: Direct permeation of dyes through P2X7 is strongly supported by the tight correlation between the charge and accessibility of the pore-lining residues and permeability of the permeant dyes (Browne et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Browne et al., 2013

claim: A larger cation, N-methyl-D-glucamine (NMDG; Mw:195 Da), becomes more permeable over time during ATP application in whole-cell patch clamp experiments.
source: Dilation of the P2X7 membrane pore is corroborated based on the observation that a larger cation, N-methyl-D-glucamine (NMDG; Mw:195 Da), becomes more permeable over time during ATP application in whole-cell patch clamp experiments (Virginio et al., 1999; Yan et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Virginio et al., 1999; Yan et al., 2008

claim: Time-dependent NMDG permeability is most likely due to a consequence of unintended ion accumulation in whole-cell patch clamp experiments.
source: This P2X7 pore dilation theory, however, has also been challenged by other studies demonstrating that time-dependent NMDG permeability is most likely due to a consequence of unintended ion accumulation in whole-cell patch clamp experiments (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2015

claim: The unitary conductance of the P2X7 receptor remains constant over time.
source: Furthermore, studies using single channel recordings provided compelling evidence that the unitary conductance of the P2X7 receptor remains constant over time (Riedel et al., 2007; Harkat et al., 2017; Pippel et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Riedel et al., 2007; Harkat et al., 2017; Pippel et al., 2017

claim: The P2X7 receptor immediately opens a pore that is large enough for NMDG to permeate.
source: These studies disagree with the pore-dilation model and suggest that the P2X7 receptor immediately opens a pore that is large enough for NMDG to permeate.
evidence: Inferred from single channel recording studies cited (Riedel et al., 2007; Harkat et al., 2017; Pippel et al., 2017)

claim: Dye-uptake strictly depends on the unique C-terminal domain of P2X7.
source: Setting aside the controversial building block of the P2X7 triggered dye-permeable pore, it has been consistently reported that dye-uptake strictly depends on its unique C-terminal domain (CTD), which exists only in the P2X7 subtype (~250 AA).
evidence: Supported by general reference to consistent reports in the literature

claim: Cells expressing C-terminally truncated versions of the P2X7 receptor fail to take up large molecules, while small cations (e.g. Na+ and Ca2+) remain permeable.
source: Indeed, cells expressing C-terminally truncated versions of the P2X7 receptor fail to take up large molecules, while small cations (e.g. Na+ and Ca2+) remain permeable (Surprenant et al., 1996; Rassendren et al., 1997; Cheewatrakoolpong et al., 2005; Adinolfi et al., 2010; Cervetto et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Surprenant et al., 1996; Rassendren et al., 1997; Cheewatrakoolpong et al., 2005; Adinolfi et al., 2010; Cervetto et al., 2013

claim: The CTD harbors a number of potential binding motifs for molecules such as β-arrestin, bacterial lipopolysaccharide, calmodulin, and kinases.
source: While the primary sequence of the CTD is dissimilar to those of any known proteins, it harbors a number of potential binding motifs for molecules such as β-arrestin, bacterial lipopolysaccharide, calmodulin, and kinases (Denlinger et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2001; Roger et al., 2008; Roger et al., 2010; Costa-Junior et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Denlinger et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2001; Roger et al., 2008; Roger et al., 2010; Costa-Junior et al., 2011

claim: The CTD has been suggested to be involved in proper assembly and trafficking.
source: It has also been suggested to be involved in proper assembly and trafficking (Denlinger et al., 2003; Smart et al., 2003; Gonnord et al., 2009; Bradley et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Denlinger et al., 2003; Smart et al., 2003; Gonnord et al., 2009; Bradley et al., 2010

claim: There is a stretch of 18 amino acid residues rich in cysteine (six cysteines) located at the beginning of the CTD, right after the second transmembrane helix.
source: Interestingly, there is a stretch of 18 amino acid residues rich in cysteine (six cysteines) located at the beginning of the CTD (Figure 1A), right after the second transmembrane helix.
evidence: Directly stated in text and shown in Figure 1A

claim: The Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in lipid raft association.
source: This Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in lipid raft association (Gonnord et al., 2009), cholesterol binding (Robinson et al., 2014; Murrell-Lagnado, 2017), and channel gating (Allsopp and Evans, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gonnord et al., 2009

claim: The Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in cholesterol binding.
source: This Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in lipid raft association (Gonnord et al., 2009), cholesterol binding (Robinson et al., 2014; Murrell-Lagnado, 2017), and channel gating (Allsopp and Evans, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robinson et al., 2014; Murrell-Lagnado, 2017

claim: The Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in channel gating.
source: This Cys-rich region (CRR) has been proposed to play major roles in lipid raft association (Gonnord et al., 2009), cholesterol binding (Robinson et al., 2014; Murrell-Lagnado, 2017), and channel gating (Allsopp and Evans, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Allsopp and Evans, 2015

claim: Truncated versions of pdP2X7 at the N-terminus (ΔN; Δ1–22) or at the C-terminus (ΔC; Δ360–600) diminished the YO-PRO-1 uptake by more than 10 fold compared to the full-length receptor.
source: When expressed in HEK293 cells, truncated versions of pdP2X7 at the N-terminus (ΔN; Δ1–22) or at the C-terminus (ΔC; Δ360–600) diminished the YO-PRO-1 uptake by more than 10 fold compared to the full-length receptor (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: When both termini were truncated (ΔNC), there was no detectable YO-PRO-1 uptake.
source: When both termini were truncated (ΔNC), there was no detectable YO-PRO-1 uptake (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: Surface biotinylation experiments showed that the expression levels of truncated receptors were comparable or even slightly higher for ΔC.
source: Surface biotinylation experiments showed that the expression levels of truncated receptors were comparable or even slightly higher for ΔC, suggesting that the diminished ATP-triggered YO-PRO-1 uptake was due to reduced channel activity but not due to lower surface expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D

claim: The diminished ATP-triggered YO-PRO-1 uptake was due to reduced channel activity but not due to lower surface expression.
source: Surface biotinylation experiments showed that the expression levels of truncated receptors were comparable or even slightly higher for ΔC, suggesting that the diminished ATP-triggered YO-PRO-1 uptake was due to reduced channel activity but not due to lower surface expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: Inferred from surface biotinylation data shown in Figure 1D

claim: Current densities from whole-cell patch clamp recordings revealed that the degree of current reduction was only ~50% for ΔN, and both ΔC and ΔNC gave rise to currents that were less than ~10% of the full-length channel.
source: Current densities from whole-cell patch clamp recordings revealed a similar pattern, though the degree of current reduction was only ~50% for ΔN, and both ΔC and ΔNC gave rise to currents that were less than ~10% of the full-length channel (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The CTD and the NTD play important roles in both dye-uptake and small ion permeation in HEK293 cells.
source: These results suggest that the CTD and the NTD (though to a lesser extent) play important roles in both dye-uptake and small ion permeation in HEK293 cells.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on truncated constructs

claim: Orientation of the reconstituted pdP2X7-ΔNC was mostly outside-out.
source: Orientation of the reconstituted pdP2X7-ΔNC was mostly outside-out, as externally applied recombinant EndoH removed the extracellular carbohydrates attached through posttranslational glycosylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: When pdP2X7-ΔNC containing liposomes were treated with ATP, the Ca2+ signal increased in a dose-dependent manner.
source: When pdP2X7-ΔNC containing liposomes were treated with ATP, the Ca2+ signal increased in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C

claim: The apparent low channel activity of pdP2X7-ΔNC in these experiments is likely due to the diminished concentrations of free ATP (ATP4-) resulting from the formation of calcium-ATP complexes.
source: The apparent low channel activity of pdP2X7-ΔNC in these experiments is likely due to the diminished concentrations of free ATP (ATP4-) resulting from the formation of calcium-ATP complexes.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations and knowledge of calcium-ATP complex formation

claim: EC50 of the calculated free ATP was 29 μM, which was comparable with that obtained for the crystallized version of pdP2X7 (pdP2X7-cryst; EC50: 40 μM) in whole-cell recordings without calcium in the extracellular solution.
source: Indeed, EC50 of the calculated free ATP was 29 μM, which was comparable with that obtained for the crystallized version of pdP2X7 (pdP2X7-cryst; EC50: 40 μM) in whole-cell recordings without calcium in the extracellular solution (Karasawa and Kawate, 2016).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citation to Karasawa and Kawate, 2016

claim: The P2X7 receptor, like the P2X2 and 4 subtypes, requires free ATP for its activation.
source: This suggests that the P2X7 receptor, like the P2X2 and 4 subtypes, requires free ATP for its activation (Klapperstück et al., 2001; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: Inferred from experimental data and supported by citations to Klapperstück et al., 2001; Li et al., 2013

claim: The ATP dose-dependent Ca2+-uptake indicates that the reconstituted pdP2X7-ΔNC is functional and both the NTD and the CTD are not required for permeation by small cations.
source: The ATP dose-dependent Ca2+-uptake indicates that the reconstituted pdP2X7-ΔNC is functional and both the NTD and the CTD are not required for permeation by small cations.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data on Ca2+ uptake

claim: The liposomes reconstituted with pdP2X7-ΔNC presented a robust YO-PRO-1 uptake in a dose dependent manner.
source: To our surprise, the liposomes reconstituted with pdP2X7-ΔNC presented a robust YO-PRO-1 uptake in a dose dependent manner (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F

claim: There was no time-lag in YO-PRO-1 uptake after ATP application and the response was monophasic.
source: There was no time-lag in YO-PRO-1 uptake after ATP application and the response was monophasic.
evidence: Observed from experimental data

claim: The Hill coefficient was 2.7 and the EC50 was 21 μM for YO-PRO-1 uptake, which were comparable with the Ca2+ uptake assay.
source: The Hill coefficient was 2.7 and the EC50 was 21 μM, which were comparable with the Ca2+ uptake assay (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C

claim: pdP2X7 alone is sufficient to form a membrane pore large enough for YO-PRO-1 to permeate and that neither N- or C-terminus is required for this process.
source: These results demonstrate that pdP2X7 alone is sufficient to form a membrane pore large enough for YO-PRO-1 to permeate and that neither N- or C-terminus is required for this process.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on pdP2X7-ΔNC in liposomes

claim: The immediate and monophasic increase of the fluorescence signal indicate that pore dilation is unlikely.
source: Furthermore, the immediate and monophasic increase of the fluorescence signal indicate that pore dilation is unlikely.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations

claim: In HEK lipids, uptake of Ca2+ or YO-PRO-1 by pdP2X7-ΔNC was drastically attenuated.
source: In those lipids, uptake of Ca2+ or YO-PRO-1 by pdP2X7-ΔNC was drastically attenuated (Figure 3A and B), which was in contrast to the robust channel activity in lipids containing only POPE and POPG (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B

claim: A component of the HEK lipid mixture antagonizes P2X7 function.
source: These results support the idea that a component of the HEK lipid mixture antagonizes P2X7 function.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results comparing different lipid compositions

claim: Only weak YO-PRO-1 uptake activity was observed with the control liposomes composed of 50% POPC and 50% POPE.
source: Remarkably, only weak YO-PRO-1 uptake activity was observed with the control liposomes composed of 50% POPC and 50% POPE (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D

claim: When the liposomes contained 50% POPG or SM, YO-PRO-1 uptake was substantially enhanced.
source: Conversely, when the liposomes contained 50% POPG or SM, YO-PRO-1 uptake was substantially enhanced.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: POPG especially boosted the YO-PRO-1 uptake by ~7 fold compared to the control.
source: POPG especially boosted the YO-PRO-1 uptake by ~7 fold compared to the control.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: POPG and SM facilitate the activity of pdP2X7-ΔNC and POPE, POPC, and cholesterol counteract the facilitating action of those lipids.
source: These results suggest that POPG and SM facilitate the activity of pdP2X7-ΔNC and that POPE, POPC, and cholesterol counteract the facilitating action of those lipids.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on different lipid compositions

claim: Cholesterol seems to be the dominant antagonist of pdP2X7-ΔNC in the HEK lipids.
source: Cholesterol therefore seems to be the dominant antagonist of pdP2X7-ΔNC in the HEK lipids.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on lipid compositions

claim: The liposomes without cholesterol showed as strong YO-PRO-1 uptake as the POPE/POPG liposomes.
source: The liposomes without cholesterol showed as strong YO-PRO-1 uptake as the POPE/POPG liposomes (Figure 4A and B), consistent with the idea that POPG and SM facilitate P2X7 channel activity.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B

claim: Less dye-uptake was observed as the concentration of cholesterol increased until it reached 15% where the inhibitory effect saturated.
source: As we expected, we observed less dye-uptake as the concentration of cholesterol increased until it reached 15% where the inhibitory effect saturated (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B

claim: The inhibitory action of cholesterol can be seen at a concentration as low as 5% and the inhibitory effect saturates around 15%.
source: These results indicate that the inhibitory action of cholesterol can be seen at a concentration as low as 5% and that the inhibitory effect saturates around 15%.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data on cholesterol concentration effects

claim: P2X7 receptor activity depends heavily on lipid compositions.
source: Altogether, our results demonstrate that P2X7 receptor activity depends heavily on lipid compositions.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on various lipid compositions

claim: Concentrations of POPG, SM, and cholesterol seem to play important roles in regulating the P2X7 receptor activity.
source: Especially, concentrations of POPG, SM, and cholesterol seem to play important roles in regulating the P2X7 receptor activity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on lipid compositions

claim: DPH anisotropy increased as the concentration of cholesterol increased from 0% to 25% in liposomes composed of HEK lipids.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, DPH anisotropy increased as the concentration of cholesterol increased from 0% to 25% in liposomes composed of HEK lipids.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B

claim: Cholesterol enhances membrane rigidity in a dose dependent manner.
source: This suggests that cholesterol indeed enhances membrane rigidity in a dose dependent manner.
evidence: Inferred from DPH anisotropy data

claim: No significant fluorescence anisotropy was observed when DPH was incubated with the liposomes enriched with POPC, POPE, POPS, or POPG.
source: In contrast, no significant fluorescence anisotropy was observed when DPH was incubated with the liposomes enriched with POPC, POPE, POPS, or POPG (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C

claim: The SM-enriched liposome increased the level of DPH anisotropy, indicating that SM also enhances the membrane rigidity.
source: Notably, the SM-enriched liposome increased the level of DPH anisotropy, indicating that SM also enhances the membrane rigidity.
evidence: Supported by experimental data and inference

claim: Membrane rigidity per se unlikely regulates the P2X7 receptor activity.
source: Because SM-enriched liposomes facilitate the channel activity of pdP2X7-ΔNC (Figure 3D), this result suggests that membrane rigidity per se unlikely regulates the P2X7 receptor activity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on SM and channel activity

claim: Linear regression analysis revealed no significant correlation (R2 = 0.044) between DPH anisotropy and YO-PRO-1 uptake activity in the absence of cholesterol.
source: Supporting this, linear regression analysis revealed no significant correlation (R2 = 0.044) between DPH anisotropy and YO-PRO-1 uptake activity in the absence of cholesterol (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 5D

claim: The inhibitory effect of cholesterol derives from an alternative mechanism and the increased membrane rigidity probably plays a lesser role, if any.
source: These results indicate that the inhibitory effect of cholesterol derives from an alternative mechanism and that the increased membrane rigidity probably plays a lesser role, if any.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on membrane rigidity and channel activity

claim: The fluorescence emission spectrum showed substantial increase in fluorescence when 22-NBD-cholesterol was incubated with pdP2X7-ΔNC.
source: The fluorescence emission spectrum showed substantial increase in fluorescence when 22-NBD-cholesterol was incubated with pdP2X7-ΔNC (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B

claim: The enhanced fluorescence was due to the 22-NBD-cholesterol binding to pdP2X7-ΔNC but not to detergent micelles.
source: The no protein control showed much weaker fluorescence, suggesting that the enhanced fluorescence was due to the 22-NBD-cholesterol binding to pdP2X7-ΔNC but not to detergent micelles.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data comparing protein and no-protein controls

claim: Binding of 22-NBD-cholesterol to pdP2X7-ΔNC was dose-dependent, supporting specific interactions between cholesterol and pdP2X7-ΔNC.
source: Importantly, binding of 22-NBD-cholesterol to pdP2X7-ΔNC was dose-dependent, supporting specific interactions between cholesterol and pdP2X7-ΔNC (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C

claim: Cholesterol inhibits pdP2X7-ΔNC by directly interacting with its transmembrane domain, rather than by indirectly changing the membrane fluidity.
source: Together, these results suggest that cholesterol inhibits pdP2X7-ΔNC by directly interacting with its transmembrane domain, rather than by indirectly changing the membrane fluidity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on cholesterol binding and membrane rigidity

claim: A deletion of the 18 amino-acid Cys-rich region (CRR) in hP2X7 diminishes its channel activity without affecting the surface expression.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that a deletion of the 18 amino-acid Cys-rich region (CRR) in hP2X7 diminishes its channel activity without affecting the surface expression, suggesting an important role of the CRR in P2X7 activity (Robinson et al., 2014; Allsopp and Evans, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robinson et al., 2014; Allsopp and Evans, 2015

claim: The CRR-deficient rat P2X7 receptor maintains full channel activity.
source: However, another study proposed otherwise; the CRR-deficient rat P2X7 receptor maintains full channel activity (Jiang et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2005

claim: When the level of cholesterol was reduced by treating HEK293 cells with methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MCD), YO-PRO-1 uptake dramatically increased with the constructs that include the CRR.
source: When the level of cholesterol was reduced by treating HEK293 cells with methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MCD), YO-PRO-1 uptake dramatically increased with the constructs that include the CRR (i.e. full-length, ΔN, and ΔNC+CRR).
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: The effect of MCD was cholesterol dependent, as no significant enhancement in dye-uptake was observed when pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRR was expressed in insect Sf9 cells that lack cholesterol in the plasma membrane.
source: The effect of MCD was cholesterol dependent, as no significant enhancement in dye-uptake was observed when pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRR was expressed in insect Sf9 cells that lack cholesterol in the plasma membrane (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B

claim: In Sf9 cells, pdP2X7-ΔNC presented strong YO-PRO-1 uptake activity, consistent with reconstitution experiments in the absence of cholesterol.
source: In those cells, pdP2X7-ΔNC presented strong YO-PRO-1 uptake activity, consistent with our reconstitution experiments in the absence of cholesterol (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and consistency with previous results

claim: Strong YO-PRO-1 uptake was observed for ΔNC + CRRa, b, and c, but further truncated constructs (CRRd and e) showed much weaker activity.
source: Whereas strong YO-PRO-1 uptake was observed for ΔNC + CRRa, b, and c, further truncated constructs (CRRd and e) showed much weaker activity (Figure 8B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B

claim: The first nine residues in CRR (i.e. between C362 to C370) harbor an essential element for facilitating P2X7 receptor channel activity.
source: These results indicate that the first nine residues in CRR (i.e. between C362 to C370) harbor an essential element for facilitating P2X7 receptor channel activity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on truncation constructs

claim: The cysteine mutants outside of the first nine amino acids in CRR (i.e. C373S, C374S, and C377S) all showed strong channel activity.
source: Consistent with the dye-uptake experiments using the truncation constructs, the cysteine mutants outside of the first nine amino acids in CRR (i.e. C373S, C374S, and C377S) all showed strong channel activity (Figure 8C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C

claim: The C362S or C363S mutants showed ~40% to 60% less activity than P2X7-ΔNC+CRR.
source: In contrast, the C362S or C363S mutants showed ~40% to 60% less activity than P2X7-ΔNC+CRR.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: The C370S mutant presented a strong channel activity despite that the truncation of the CRR before this residue (CRRd) reduced the dye-uptake by more than 50%.
source: Interestingly, the C370S mutant presented a strong channel activity despite that the truncation of the CRR before this residue (CRRd) reduced the dye-uptake by more than 50% (Figure 8B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B

claim: When both C362S and C363S were combined, the channel activity was almost completely abolished.
source: When both C362S and C363S were combined, the channel activity was almost completely abolished (Figure 8C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C

claim: None of the individual cysteines were essential, but C362 and C363 play dominant roles in facilitating the P2X7 receptor activity.
source: These results indicate that none of the individual cysteines were essential, but C362 and C363 play dominant roles in facilitating the P2X7 receptor activity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on cysteine mutants

claim: When C362 and C363 were mutated to serines in the full-length pdP2X7 receptor, no YO-PRO-1 activity was observed.
source: Indeed, when these two cysteine residues were mutated to serines in the full-length pdP2X7 receptor, no YO-PRO-1 activity was observed (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A

claim: The C363A mutant of hP2X7 showed little dye-uptake.
source: This result was consistent with the C363A mutant of hP2X7, which also showed little dye-uptake (Robinson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Robinson et al., 2014

claim: The surface expression was unaffected by the C362S/C363S mutations.
source: Because the surface expression was unaffected by the C362S/C363S mutations, it is likely that these cysteines play roles in enhancing P2X7 channel opening, rather than affecting trafficking or assembly (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B

claim: C362 and C363 play roles in enhancing P2X7 channel opening, rather than affecting trafficking or assembly.
source: Because the surface expression was unaffected by the C362S/C363S mutations, it is likely that these cysteines play roles in enhancing P2X7 channel opening, rather than affecting trafficking or assembly (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Inferred from experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B

claim: Multiple cysteine residues in the CTD, including the ones in CRR, have been suggested to be posttranslationally modified by palmitoylation.
source: Multiple cysteine residues in the CTD, including the ones in CRR, have been suggested to be posttranslationally modified by palmitoylation (Gonnord et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gonnord et al., 2009

claim: pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc is heavily modified with 17-ODYA, which resulted in a much stronger fluorescence than RalA.
source: We found that pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc is heavily modified with 17-ODYA, which resulted in a much stronger fluorescence than RalA (Figure 9).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9

claim: The cysteine residues in CRRc are likely palmitoylated.
source: Because the pdP2X7-ΔNC, which is only nine amino acids shorter than pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc was not modified by 17-ODYA, it is likely that the cysteine residues in CRRc are indeed palmitoylated (Figure 9).
evidence: Inferred from experimental data shown in Figure 9

claim: Palmitoylation of at least one of the C362, C363, C370 plays an important role in enhancing the P2X7 channel activity.
source: In combination with the cysteine mutagenesis study, these results suggest that palmitoylation of at least one of the C362, C363, C370 plays an important role in enhancing the P2X7 channel activity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on palmitoylation and mutagenesis

claim: Palmitoylation of CRR in the C-terminus facilitates the channel opening of the P2X7 receptor, which contributes to counteract the inhibitory effect of cholesterol in the plasma membrane.
source: Altogether, our results demonstrated that palmitoylation of CRR in the C-terminus facilitates the channel opening of the P2X7 receptor, which contributes to counteract the inhibitory effect of cholesterol in the plasma membrane.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on palmitoylation, CRR, and cholesterol

claim: The P2X7 receptor itself constitutes a dye-permeable pore.
source: In this study, we investigated the channel activity of purified pdP2X7 reconstituted into liposomes in the absence of other cellular components. In contrast to previous studies, we demonstrated that pdP2X7 forms a pore independent of either the CTD or the NTD. This result also provides strong evidence that the P2X7 receptor on its own constitutes a dye-permeable pore.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on purified and reconstituted P2X7

claim: The P2X7 receptor does not require the CTD for its channel activity itself, but it does depend on the CTD for counteracting the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
source: These results highlight that the P2X7 receptor does not require the CTD for its channel activity itself, but it does depend on the CTD for counteracting the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on truncated constructs and cholesterol effects

claim: Cholesterol directly interacts with a P2X7 receptor that lacks both N- and C-terminus, indicating that cholesterol likely inhibits channel activity by binding to the transmembrane helices.
source: Our in vitro binding assay revealed that cholesterol directly interacts with a P2X7 receptor that lacks both N- and C-terminus, indicating that cholesterol likely inhibits channel activity by binding to the transmembrane helices.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on cholesterol binding to pdP2X7-ΔNC

claim: A cholesterol-dependent increase in membrane rigidity is not the primary mechanism of inhibition.
source: We also demonstrated that a cholesterol-dependent increase in membrane rigidity is not the primary mechanism of inhibition, as a P2X7 facilitating lipid SM also increases membrane rigidity.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on membrane rigidity and channel activity

claim: The immediate and monophasic dye uptake supports that the pore of the P2X7 receptor does not dilate.
source: Dye uptake activity in the absence of other channels strongly support that the P2X7 receptor itself constitutes a dye-permeable pore. Also, the immediate and monophasic dye uptake supports that the pore of the P2X7 receptor does not dilate.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations of dye uptake kinetics

claim: NMDG-mediated currents are readily recorded from P2X7 receptor expressing cells without prolonged or repeated application of ATP.
source: This is consistent with the recent studies demonstrating that NMDG-mediated currents are readily recorded from P2X7 receptor expressing cells without prolonged or repeated application of ATP (Harkat et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harkat et al., 2017

claim: Other P2X receptor subtypes including P2X2-4 also give rise to NMDG-mediated currents.
source: Interestingly, those studies demonstrated that other P2X receptor subtypes including P2X2-4 also give rise to NMDG-mediated currents (Li et al., 2015; Harkat et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2015; Harkat et al., 2017

claim: The ability to open a dye-permeable pore may actually be a common characteristic of P2X receptors.
source: These results suggest that the ability to open a dye-permeable pore may actually be a common characteristic of P2X receptors.
evidence: Inferred from studies showing NMDG permeability in multiple P2X subtypes

claim: The currently available crystal structures present similar overall architectures of the ATP-binding extracellular region and the transmembrane channel for the P2X3, 4 and 7 subtypes.
source: Furthermore, this idea is also supported by the currently available crystal structures, which present similar overall architectures of the ATP-binding extracellular region and the transmembrane channel for the P2X3, 4 and 7 subtypes (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Karasawa and Kawate, 2016; Mansoor et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Karasawa and Kawate, 2016; Mansoor et al., 2016

claim: Permeability of a large molecule such as NMDG seems much less than that of a small ion like Na+.
source: Notably, permeability of a large molecule such as NMDG seems much less than that of a small ion like Na+, as suggested by Harkat et al. (Harkat et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harkat et al., 2017

claim: The permeability of a large molecule through the P2X7 receptor may be the highest among P2X subtypes, which could be a reason why the dye-permeable pore has been commonly observed for the P2X7 subtype.
source: This ratio may vary among the different P2X subtypes and the permeability of a large molecule through the P2X7 receptor may be the highest, which could be a reason why the dye-permeable pore has been commonly observed for the P2X7 subtype.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on experimental observations

claim: Extending the C-terminus of pdP2X7-ΔNC by just nine residues almost completely recovers the dye-uptake activity in the presence of MCD.
source: We also demonstrated that extending the C-terminus of pdP2X7-ΔNC by just nine residues almost completely recovers the dye-uptake activity in the presence of MCD.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc was efficiently labeled with a palmitic acid analogue in HEK293 cells.
source: Because this construct (pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc) was efficiently labeled with a palmitic acid analogue in HEK293 cells, it is likely that the facilitating function of CRR derives from palmitoylation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: The facilitating function of CRR derives from palmitoylation.
source: Because this construct (pdP2X7-ΔNC+CRRc) was efficiently labeled with a palmitic acid analogue in HEK293 cells, it is likely that the facilitating function of CRR derives from palmitoylation.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data on palmitoylation

claim: Mutation of the first two cysteine residues in CRR (C362 and C363) rendered the full-length pdP2X7 incapable of dye-uptake, even in the presence of the entire CTD.
source: Indeed, mutation of the first two cysteine residues in CRR (C362 and C363) rendered the full-length pdP2X7 incapable of dye-uptake, even in the presence of the entire CTD.
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: Acylation of C362 and C363 could alter the tilting angles of TM2.
source: Given that C362 and C363 are located near the end of the second transmembrane helix (TM2), we speculate that acylation of these two cysteines could alter the tilting angles of TM2.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on structural considerations

claim: Palmitoylated cysteines may serve as an intracellular anchor, which may facilitate the movement required for P2X7 channel opening.
source: Alternatively, palmitoylated cysteines may serve as an intracellular anchor, which may facilitate the movement required for P2X7 channel opening.
evidence: Speculative reasoning

claim: Attached fatty acids may interact with cholesterol bound to the transmembrane helices of the P2X7 receptor, which may reduce the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
source: It is also possible that attached fatty acids may interact with cholesterol bound to the transmembrane helices of the P2X7 receptor, which may reduce the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
evidence: Speculative reasoning

claim: A similar mechanism has been proposed for the μ-opioid receptor, whose homodimer may be stabilized through direct interaction between cholesterol and palmitate attached to a nearby cysteine.
source: A similar mechanism has been proposed for the μ-opioid receptor, whose homodimer may be stabilized through direct interaction between cholesterol and palmitate attached to a nearby cysteine (Zheng et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zheng et al., 2012

claim: P2X7 channel opening is facilitated by POPG or SM but not by other common lipids in plasma membrane such as POPC or POPS.
source: By systematically testing different types of lipids, we discovered that P2X7 channel opening is facilitated by POPG or SM but not by other common lipids in plasma membrane such as POPC or POPS.
evidence: Supported by experimental data on lipid compositions

claim: POPG is a minor component (typically less than 2% of total lipids) for most neuronal and blood cells.
source: Though POPG is a minor component (typically less than 2% of total lipids) for most neuronal and blood cells (Gottfried, 1967; Cornwell et al., 1968; Calderon et al., 1995), this lipid exists at relatively high concentration (~9%) in alveolar macrophage (Sahu and Lynn, 1977).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gottfried, 1967; Cornwell et al., 1968; Calderon et al., 1995; Sahu and Lynn, 1977

claim: POPG exists at relatively high concentration (~9%) in alveolar macrophage.
source: Though POPG is a minor component (typically less than 2% of total lipids) for most neuronal and blood cells (Gottfried, 1967; Cornwell et al., 1968; Calderon et al., 1995), this lipid exists at relatively high concentration (~9%) in alveolar macrophage (Sahu and Lynn, 1977).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sahu and Lynn, 1977

claim: Macrophages only contain ~8% cholesterol in the membrane.
source: Considering that macrophages only contain ~8% cholesterol in the membrane (Sahu and Lynn, 1977), the inhibitory action by cholesterol is probably weaker in these cells.
evidence: Supported by citation to Sahu and Lynn, 1977

claim: The inhibitory action by cholesterol is probably weaker in macrophages.
source: Considering that macrophages only contain ~8% cholesterol in the membrane (Sahu and Lynn, 1977), the inhibitory action by cholesterol is probably weaker in these cells.
evidence: Inferred from cholesterol content in macrophages

claim: POPG has been shown to be up-regulated in lymphoma cells that overexpress the v-myc avian myelocytomatosis viral oncogene homolog.
source: Also, POPG has been shown to be up-regulated in lymphoma cells that overexpress the v-myc avian myelocytomatosis viral oncogene homolog (Eberlin et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Eberlin et al., 2014

claim: Up-regulation of POPG provides another potential mechanism for P2X7 receptor hyper-activation, which has been implicated in different types of cancer.
source: While it is uncertain whether up-regulation of POPG is a common phenomenon for other cancer cells, it provides another potential mechanism for P2X7 receptor hyper-activation, which has been implicated in different types of cancer (Di Virgilio et al., 2009; Roger and Pelegrin, 2011; Adinolfi et al., 2012).
evidence: Speculative reasoning supported by citations to Di Virgilio et al., 2009; Roger and Pelegrin, 2011; Adinolfi et al., 2012

claim: SM is a major lipid in the plasma membrane; however, SM content highly varies from cell to cell.
source: In contrast to POPG, SM is a major lipid in the plasma membrane; however, SM content highly varies from cell to cell.
evidence: General knowledge about lipid composition

claim: Red blood cells contain 20–30% SM.
source: For example, red blood cells contain 20–30% SM (Cornwell et al., 1968) but lymphoblasts contain only 4% (Gottfried, 1967).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cornwell et al., 1968

claim: Lymphoblasts contain only 4% SM.
source: For example, red blood cells contain 20–30% SM (Cornwell et al., 1968) but lymphoblasts contain only 4% (Gottfried, 1967).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gottfried, 1967

claim: Activation of P2X7 receptors have been demonstrated to activate acid sphingomyelinase in microglia, which is responsible for degrading SM in the plasma membrane and triggering IL-1β release.
source: Interestingly, activation of P2X7 receptors have been demonstrated to activate acid sphingomyelinase in microglia, which is responsible for degrading SM in the plasma membrane and triggering IL-1β release (Bianco et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bianco et al., 2009

claim: Deficiency in acid sphingomyelinase leads to the devastating Niemann-Pick disease that is associated with severe cognitive decline and impaired neuromotor coordination.
source: Notably, deficiency in acid sphingomyelinase leads to the devastating Niemann-Pick disease that is associated with severe cognitive decline and impaired neuromotor coordination (Ledesma et al., 2011; Rigante et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ledesma et al., 2011; Rigante et al., 2017

claim: Accumulation of SM due to the lack of acid sphingomyelinase activity may hyper-activate P2X7 receptors.
source: Though the exact mechanism remains poorly understood, it is possible that accumulation of SM due to the lack of acid sphingomyelinase activity may hyper-activate P2X7 receptors.
evidence: Speculative reasoning

claim: Cholesterol also diminishes channel activity of the full-length P2X7.
source: Nevertheless, the previous studies by the Murrell-Lagnado group (Robinson et al., 2014) and our cell-based studies using MCD demonstrate that cholesterol also diminishes channel activity of the full-length P2X7.
evidence: Supported by citation to Robinson et al., 2014 and experimental data

claim: The inhibitory effect of cholesterol is not limited to P2X7-ΔNC but also present for the WT P2X7.
source: These experiments indicate that the inhibitory effect of cholesterol is not limited to P2X7-ΔNC but also present for the WT P2X7.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on full-length P2X7

claim: The P2X7 receptor harbors an intrinsic dye-permeable pore whose activity depends substantially on lipid composition.
source: In conclusion, we have demonstrated that the P2X7 receptor harbors an intrinsic dye-permeable pore whose activity depends substantially on lipid composition.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results throughout the study

claim: It is unlikely that the P2X7 specific CTD constitutes a pore or recruits other pore-forming proteins.
source: Because transmembrane helices of the P2X7 receptor are sufficient for the formation of the dye-permeable pore, it is unlikely that the P2X7 specific CTD constitutes a pore or recruits other pore-forming proteins.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on pdP2X7-ΔNC

claim: The CTD facilitates P2X7 channel activity through palmitoylated cysteines near the end of the pore-lining helix, which contributes to counteract the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
source: The CTD instead facilitates its channel activity through palmitoylated cysteines near the end of the pore-lining helix, which contributes to counteract the inhibitory effect of cholesterol.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on CRR and palmitoylation

claim: Activation of P2X7 receptors considerably varies depending on the host cells, which may be a plausible explanation for inconsistent results from previous functional studies.
source: These novel insights imply that activation of P2X7 receptors considerably varies depending on the host cells, which may be a plausible explanation for inconsistent results from previous functional studies.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results on lipid-dependent activity
